title: The Pólya–Vinogradov inequality with log log q for every character: paper, Lean 4 library and checking programs
description:
Version 4 of the paper, single column (amsart), 53 pages, with its LaTeX source, programs that check the explicit constants of the proofs, the arithmetic identities of Appendix B and the character sums for small moduli, and a Lean 4 library. The paper proves, with no hypothesis, that M(χ) ≤ C √q log log q for every primitive Dirichlet character χ modulo q ≥ 3, with an absolute constant C, where M(χ) is the largest modulus of a partial sum of χ, and that |L'/L(1, χ)| ≤ C log log q for every nonprincipal character. This is the bound that Montgomery and Vaughan deduced from the generalised Riemann hypothesis, sharp up to the constant by a theorem of Paley. The proof combines a transfer theorem for a single character with the zero-free half-plane Re s > 11/12 for all finite-order Hecke L-functions over Q(√−3), and so for all Dirichlet L-functions; the half-plane and its proof are due to OpenAI (The quasi-Riemann hypothesis: a cubic theta argument with a fixed ray class character, 5 October 2026), and Appendix B gives the proof in full with every external input a published theorem. New in this version: the Euler–Kronecker constant γ_m of Q(ζ_m) satisfies γ_m ≤ 12 log m + 36 log log m + C for every m ≥ 3, an order known before only under the generalised Riemann hypothesis, and γ_q ≥ −C log q log log q for primes q. From Chebyshev's bounds alone, at most q^ε characters modulo q violate the bounds for M(χ) and L'/L(1, χ). OpenAI's Lean 4 proof of the wider half-plane Re s > 7/8 is compiled from source and checked by the Lean kernel in this repository as an independent check; nothing in the paper uses it.

The results were first made public on 15 October 2026 as release v1.0.0 of this repository (concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23383715). Version 3 (10.5281/zenodo.23672710) is hexagon:2610.00256v3; this version replaces it on Hexagon.
